Florida State Seminoles Louisville Cardinals NCAAF Louisville looks to get back on track following a second straight loss in ACC play when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium tonight at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville predictions and college football picks for Friday, Oct. 9 expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Florida State +4.5 Florida State vs Louisville prop: Florida State team total Over 27.5 Florida State has scored 28+ points in four of five games this season, and Louisville has allowed 28+ points to all four of its FBS opponents this season. I'd play the Over on the Seminoles' team total at 27.5 or better . The Seminoles are averaging 33.2 ppg this season, and Kromah has quickly become one of the best running backs in the country. He ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles on runs (28) and runs of 10+ yards (14). Daniels' mobility has opened up the offense, too, with the Auburn transfer sitting top 25 in the country in QBR (80.5) thanks to the damage he's doing on the ground. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Louisville Cardinals | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 9, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football Can FSU win their third straight against Louisville to go 4-2 on the season? The Florida State Seminoles are traveling to Kentucky to meet the Louisville Cardinals for another ACC Friday Night Lights game at the L&N Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. and will be televised on ESPN. Florida State (3-2, 1-1 ACC) leads the all-time series 18-6, including a 7-3 record at Louisville (2-3, 1-2 ACC). FSU has won the last two games against the Cardinals, including a 16-6 victory in the 2023 ACC Championship Game and a 35-31 win in their most recent regular-season matchup in Louisville in 2022. The Cardinals are 4-6 against the Seminoles since joining the ACC in 2014. The Cardinals took a second straight defeat last Saturday, dropping a 31-28 contest at NC State. All three of Louisville’s losses this season have come by three points. Seven of its last eight losses dating back to 2024 have come by three points or less. The Cardinals have eight touchdowns of 50 yards or more this season, the most of any team in FBS. Five different Louisville players have scored a touchdown of 50 yards or more this season. Louisville is averaging 486 yards per game, second-best in the ACC, and has 37 plays of 20 yards or more through five games, tied with Indiana for the most in the country. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has rushed for 158 yards on the ground this season and is tied for fifth nationally among quarterbacks with six rushing touchdowns. In the first five games, Kienholz has completed 96 of 139 of his passes for a 69.1 completion percentage, 9 touchdowns with 1 interception, and is averaging 278 yards per game. The Cardinals rushed for 231 yards in the loss at NC State, with Miami native Isaac Brown rushing for 125 yards on nine carries, his 12th 100-yard game. Keyjuan Brown leads the Cardinals in rushing with 367 yards, averaging 9.7 yards per carry. Wide receiver Tre Richardson leads the Cards with 28 receptions for 445 receiving yards and has scored three touchdowns (2 receiving, 1 rushing). The three touchdowns Richardson has scored this season have been 30, 62, and 38 yards. Of his 33 offensive touches this season, 19 have gone for at least 10 yards and nine have covered 20 yards or more. The only player in the ACC with more plays of 20 yards or more is Miami’s Malachi Toney. Tight end Jaleel Skinner has hauled in 14 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns through five games. Skinner is one of just 20 players in the FBS to have multiple 60-yard plays from scrimmage and the only tight end to do it, scoring touchdowns from 61 and 69 yards. Overall, the Cardinals rank 17th in the nation in total offense (486 yards/game), 22nd in scoring offense (38.6 points/game), T-24th in passing offense (287.4 yards/game), and 38th in rushing offense (198.6 yards/game). Similar to the Seminoles, Louisville’s defense is struggling. Linebacker J.T. Capers leads the defense with 38 tackles, followed by defensive back Kaleb Beasley with 35 tackles and 3 interceptions. The Cardinal defense ranks 125th in total defense, giving up 423 yards per game, 130th in passing yards allowed (267 yards/game), and 113th in scoring defense (29.2 points/game). Florida State is coming off its most impressive win of the season, notching a 38-7 win over Virginia last Saturday. Quarterback Ashton Daniels’ five touchdowns in the victory set an FSU record, now placing him third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns and ranked 3rd with 15.87 yards per completion, while also leading the ACC in rushing scores and in yards per completion. His 183 passing yards, career-high 136 rushing yards, and five touchdowns against Virginia make him the only FBS player since 1995 to reach those marks in a game. FSU 38, Virginia 7: Seminoles dominate Cavaliers in all three phases in blowout win FSU’s improving defense now ranks 103rd in the nation, giving up 385 yards/game, 127th in passing defense (266 yards/game), and ranked T-98th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 41% of the time on third-down attempts. However, the Noles’ defense has been decent at stopping opponents behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 3.4 sacks per game for 8th best in the nation, and 20th in tackles for loss with 7.2 TFLs per game. Louisville junior wide receiver Lawayne McCoy played two seasons at Florida State before transferring this year to Louisville. In two years with the Seminoles, McCoy played in 20 games with 33 receptions for 448 yards and three touchdowns. Florida State Director of Football Strategy/Offensive Assistant Gabe Fertitta was a quality control assistant at Louisville during the 2021 season. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Louisville Cardinals Florida State is trending as a 3.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 59.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-1, 2-3 ATS) Welp. Last week’s game is certainly making me at least consider the possibility that I was being a bit harsh about this team. Somehow, FSU enters this game with a better record than Louisville. The Seminoles haven’t won a road game since 2023, but this Louisville team is coming off back-to-back losses to Wake Forest and NC State and has a knack for making a lot of mistakes. I’m still not convinced that FSU has turned over a new leaf, but as a show of faith, I’ll give them some benefit of the doubt. Florida State 31, Louisville 27 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-1 ) FSU took down a genuinely good team in Virginia, and looking back on the Alabama game, we were probably the best punch against them up to this point that ended up losing. I’m going to go out on a pretty rickety limb here and say that FSU finally ends its 1,000+ day road losing streak and defeats Louisville. Louisville’s run defense is allowing 156.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 92nd nationally. If Wisner and company can establish the run, or if Daniels can go for five touchdowns again, it’ll be a fun time for the Seminoles. Give me FSU to pull off the “upset.” FSU 41, Louisville 31 NoleThruandThru (season record: 5-0) Louisville 41, FSU 38 Jessi Wynn (season record: 3-0) Florida State enters the matchup with momentum from a two-game winning streak, including a dominant 38-7 win over Virginia. The Seminoles looked strong on both sides of the ball, with the offense finding success in both the running and passing games. FSU has struggled on the road, but I think the confidence from this winning streak will carry over. Noles 39, Louisville 32 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-1) Like everyone else, I have to reconsider how I think the next three games will go for Florida State after last week’s win against Virginia. The Seminoles ripped through the UVA offensive line for 10 sacks, ran the quarterback effectively, and played their cleanest game in what seems like forever. They also get a break, even though they travel on a short week, by facing a reeling Louisville team that has lost two in a row. Plus, for whatever reason, FSU has played well against the Cards the last few times they have met. However, one win isn’t enough for me to trust this team, especially on the road. The defense will have its hands full against Jeff Brohm’s offense, and one week does not mean all the problems are solved. FSU keeps this game close, but a bad turnover and a back-breaking touchdown drive result in a loss. Take UL to cover and the over. UL 34, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 4-0) I need to see it to believe it when it comes to FSU on the road; Louisville’s pass rush is fierce, so a successful formula is a lot of QB power and play-action shot. Louisville is bloodied and a mess on defense, but FSU hasn’t won a road game since 2023, so…. Louisville 35 , FSU 31 Jon Marchant (season record: 4-1 ) Louisville looked like a good, solid squad, but they keep losing close games. FSU, meanwhile, looked like a completely different team from what we’ve seen since 2023. Will the real FSU please stand up? Can FSU win this game? Yes. But Friday night on the road is tough. Louisville 28 , FSU 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 4-1) Friday’s game might be a battle of which team has the ball last. There should be a decent amount of points scored on both sides, though FSU could always “struggle.” In the end, I think UL has more firepower, and old friend Lawayne McCoy makes some key plays to secure the Louisville win. Louisville 45, FSU 38 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-1, 4-1 ATS) My, how the tables turn. All of a sudden, Louisville is the team in disarray, while Florida State is coming off its best game since beating Alabama to open the 2025 season. FSU’s offense has looked very good for large stretches the last few weeks, and most of those stretches occur when Norvell simplifies the number of reads Ashton Daniels has to process. If that continues, the ‘Noles should have no problem scoring 24+ points, as they have in every game this season. Will 24 be enough? Not likely. Even in back-to-back losses, UL has put up 27 and 28 points, respectively. I need to see more than one week of good defense to believe FSU will hold UL to a season low on a short week in Louisville. So now the question becomes: can Florida State outscore the Cardinals? Call me crazy, but I say yes! FSU 34, Louisville 30 Frank DaNole (season record: 3-2) These two teams are similar in that both have decent offenses while fielding defenses that leave a lot to be desired. This will be the second game when everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are only 3.5-point underdogs as the road team for a reason. Vegas knows it, and the Seminoles know it. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed last week. The Seminoles may not dominate at all three positional units for the entire game, but in the end FSU will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Cardinal opponents. FSU Seminoles 38, Louie’s Flock 31 Perry Kostidakis (season record: 3-2, 3-2 ATS) If there was ever a time for FSU to continue its success with its front seven, it’s this game. The Cardinals’ offensive line has struggled this season, giving up two sacks (81st in the country) and 6.4 tackles for loss (121st) per game. Defensively, Louisville has struggled as much as Florida State has — its 266.8 passing yards per game allowed ranks 130th in the country (FSU is 127 with 265.6) — so even if the defensive turnaround on the Seminoles’ end was fugazi, I do have confidence in their ability to put up points after another successful offensive showing. What are the things that give me pause? Remembering the “turnaround” games from last season (Wake Forest, Virginia Tech) that weren’t really proof of anything, knowing that Papa John L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium is an intimidating place to try and snap a 10-game road losing streak, the soft factor of Louisville being motivated to snap out of its funk and the real factor of Lincoln Kienholz not just being a capable quarterback but a good dual-threat o

picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. picks.headline: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana
picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's midterms for Nebraska football following its best start since 2016. Now, the Huskers welcome Indiana to Lincoln for arguably the biggest game of the season for both teams. For Nebraska, it'll either finally get over the hump and snap its 30-game losing streak against ranked opponents or start another dreadful latter half of the season. For Indiana, it's either another win or its first loss since 2024. Though this is a matchup between two undefeated teams, the contrast is present. The Hoosiers are the defending national champions, while the Huskers still have yet to prove themselves. But other factors differentiate these teams, despite their many similarities. Though both teams have slow starts offensively, Indiana has been able to march downfield early in games, only to fall short in the red zone. For Nebraska, its early-game struggles come down to the offensive line needing time to find its footing. The Hoosiers can surely exploit that, considering they held Northwestern to 32 rushing yards on 27 carries. Now Indiana can swallow up the run again for Nebraska, whose top runner in the past two weeks has been Anthony Colandrea. The Hoosiers also got to Aiden Chiles four times, who is capable of taking off. Colandrea took two sacks against Maryland, so either he's going to be taking off or he's going to be tasting the turf a lot more against the Hoosiers. But if there is time in the pocket, Colandrea can make things happen. Indiana did allow Chiles to throw 22-of-29 for 293 yards, so Colandrea could put up similar numbers. But Colandrea isn't flawless in the air. Though he's thrown only one true interception, Colandrea has been off target at times. Josh Hoover's in a similar boat but has been clean through five games, with no interceptions. Now, with reports of winds being at 17 miles per hour come kickoff, both quarterbacks could be limited in the air. However, Hoover has been sacked six times in the last four games and has only 18 rushing yards. If the Blackshirts can pressure him, they can at least slow Indiana's passing game further. That only leaves Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. for Nebraska. The duo combined for 1,107 rushing yards on 152 carries, averaging 7.3 per carry. That is a problem for the Huskers. They allowed a few big runs against Maryland and nearly 150 total yards. So, the Hoosiers can either deliver devastating blows or just chip away at the clock to get to Nebraska's defense. But that only looks at the team's execution on plays, and there are more factors to consider. The Huskers enter the game with 43 penalties after drawing 16 last week. Though there was some controversy regarding that game, 16 penalties in a game don't just happen. Nebraska has allowed teams to continue drives due to penalties or has ended its own drives due to penalties. Indiana has only gotten 17 on the season, so that's another area the Huskers can exploit. Overall, Nebraska has multiple ways to come out on top here. If the Huskers can get the run game going and shut down Indiana's, there's a chance. But the line's struggles and penalties take away some of their advantages. Plus, with that recent history and its current issues, Nebraska needs to truly take that next step if it wants to win. But that won't happen unless it comes out like a championship-caliber team, or the Hoosiers play their worst game of the season. But this game will feel like last year's Michigan game. Indiana won't blow out the Huskers like in 2024, but it will still get the win. Indiana carries a 21-game winning streak and the pedigree of recent national championship success. Nebraska is off to its best start in a decade, but one clear issue threatens to undermine the Cornhuskers' chances against the Hoosiers. Nebraska's Biggest Problem Against Indiana Sep 12, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers running back Isaiah Mozee (22) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Bowling Green Falcons during the fourth quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Nebraska ranks near the bottom of the Big Ten in discipline, averaging 8.6 penalties per game this season. The Cornhuskers were flagged 16 times in their most recent win over Maryland, tying a school record and drawing public frustration even from their head coach. Coming in, Nebraska ranks 17th in the Big Ten in total flags thrown against it. Those flags have repeatedly stalled drives, extended opponent possessions, and handed free yards to the other side. Against a team as efficient and opportunistic as Indiana, self-inflicted wounds become magnified. Indiana commits far fewer penalties, ranking third best nationally, and protects the football at an elite level, with just one turnover, revealing a stark contrast in composure. Together, they've combined for more than 1,100 yards this season. But the overall Indiana offense is balanced and avoids costly mistakes that have plagued less disciplined teams. Defensively, Indiana ranks among the nation's very best at limiting big plays and against the run, ranking 7th in FBS and allowing 2 yards per carry. That could prove the ultimate decisive factor in the trenches. Nebraska's offense, while clearly improved and capable of big moments behind dual-threat quarterback Anthony Colandrea, will face by far its stiffest test in sustaining drives against that front. There's still plenty of work to do after this week, but beating the defending national champion – and putting an end to Indiana's 21-game winning streak – would be just the moment the program has been waiting for to show that it's headed in the right direction. Indiana hasn't been the dominant version of last year, but it's still unbeaten, it's about as tuned up as it can be, and it got its first road game out of the way with a 47-15 win over Rutgers. Yeah, this might be Nebraska's moment. It's also Curt Cignetti's moment to prove that for the Hoosiers, it's business as usual. Indiana vs Nebraska Quick Hits The Hoosiers get three home games in the next four after this, but Ohio State is up next, the road date is at Michigan, and then Minnesota and USC come to Bloomington. Nebraska goes on the road for three games in the next four dates, with a trip to Oregon before a week off to get ready for Washington. Indiana won 56-7 in 2024, but the Huskers are 6-1 in the series before that going back to a Hoosier win in 1959. How To Watch Indiana vs Nebraska Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, NE – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Indiana Will Win As you'd expect from one of the best coached teams in all of sports, Indiana doesn't mess up. It has only turned the ball over once, it's third in the nation in fewest penalties, and no one does a better job of not putting itself in tough situations. It might not be that Nebraska needs to force mistakes and can win this straight up, but it has a way of pulling away in games, helped by the takeaways. On the flip side, the Huskers were flagged 16 times in the win over Maryland and have committed the most penalties of any Big Ten team so far. Why Nebraska Will Win The Hoosiers have only been stress-tested once in the 29-23 win over Northwestern, and that was partly because Wildcat quarterback Aidan Chiles was accurate with the passing game. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea might not be Drew Brees, but he's hitting 66% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and just two picks. This has to be about the Nebraska offensive line, though. The Huskers are taking over games with the running game pushing until the dam breaks, and then games turn into routs. Indiana isn't Maryland or Bowling Green, but Michigan State is a tough-as-nails team that was the only team that held the Huskers to under 200 yards, and it still lost by 18. Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines Can Nebraska get close to 40 carries? Part of the problem against Indiana is that teams have to give up on the run because it doesn't work. Only North Texas has been able to get past 66 yards this season, and it's also the only team that ran more than 35 times. North Texas also lost 52-16. The energy of the moment will carry the Huskers to a solid first half, but they won't be able to pull away. Eventually, the Nebraska run defense will start to buckle, the IU pass rush will get to Colandrea, and the hype for the Ohio State game will start about 30 seconds after the final gun. away.headline: Riley Van Poppel injury threatens Nebraska where Indiana can hurt it most
away.blurb: Considering that Van Poppel looked like he wasn't adjusting all that well to Aurich's defense in fall camp and then surged into a situation where he was getting as many snaps as any defensive lineman in the last few weeks, it couldn't be a worse time for an injury to keep him out of Saturday morning's massive game. The good for Nebraska heading into the massive showdown against Indiana on Saturday is that the team is mostly healthy. Jamal Rule, Jacory Barney, and Mekhi Nelson are off the injury reports entirely. The bad news is that Thursday night's report added a defensive player the Huskers can scarcely afford to miss. Riley Van Poppel's apparent injury isn't a big deal simply because he's a defensive lineman, and the Hoosiers' run game is easily the best the Huskers have faced so far this year. His potential absence is also a big issue because Van Poppel's playing time has increased as the season has gone on. Van Poppel's use by Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich has, in fact, never been bigger than it has been since Nebraska started Big Ten play. Against Ohio, he saw just 30 snaps. Against Bowling Green, it was down to 18, and he had just 28 snaps against North Dakota. However, he tallied 46 snaps against Michigan State and 44last week against Maryland. Riley Van Poppel injury could weaken Nebraska football front against Indiana running backs Van Poppel hasn't always been on the stat sheet. He has just 7 tackles, but 2 of those were sacks. He's also got 9 quarterback pressures, including 5 in Big Ten games alone. While his 2 sacks came in non-conference play, he's shown he can make an impact in the trenches, with 2 quarterback hurries and a quarterback hit against the Spartans and 2 more hurries against the Terrapins. "I think I'm playing probably the best I have in four years right now," Van Poppel said after Nebraska's Week 4 win over Michigan State . Van Poppel has also been a vocal leader for Nebraska, especially after earning a single-digit jersey last year and being given the option of keeping it this fall. Instead of once again wearing No. 5, he went back to his No. 44, saying he didn't believe he lived up to his own standard of what a player wearing a single digit jersey should be like. “He (Rhule) gave me the option to keep one, but I don’t see it that way. I want the guys who were truly voted to be the single digits, and if I need to go back to a different number, at the end of the day, it’s a number.” As is the policy with the Big Ten Availability Reports, it's not a guarantee that Riley Van Poppel will miss Nebraska's biggest game of the year. The Huskers will release two more before game time. One report will update the status of injured players on Friday night, and another two hours before kickoff. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. Arizona (4-1, 1-1 in Big 12) now heads out to the country roads of West Virginia, where they will face a high-scoring Mountaineers squad in the midst of a two-game losing streak. West Virginia bullied then No. 25 Virginia, 38-27, in Week 3 to build momentum heading into Big 12 play. Things haven't gone well for coach Rich Rodriguez's team since then, however, with an ugly 41-24 home loss to Oklahoma State followed by a shootout at Iowa State that ended in a 45-42 defeat after Cyclones running back Aiden Flora scored his fifth touchdown with 1:57 left in the fourth quarter. Cincinnati presented a challenge for Arizona's run defense, a challenge the Wildcats more than met after holding the Bearcats to a season-low 87 yards on the ground. Now they'll level up against the best rushing attack in the country. WVU has 1,470 rushing yards on the season, which not only leads the FBS but is 133 yards more than second place, Army, and 190 yards more than the next high major team in South Carolina. West Virginia's 294 rushing yards per game is third in the FBS, and its 17 rushing touchdowns is tied for third. A big part of the ground attack for the Mountaineers is the dual-threat ability of quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., who has a whopping 574 rushing yards and 11(!) rushing touchdowns on the season - which is tied with Florida running back Jadan Baugh for the most in the country. Hawkins is good in the air as well, with 836 passing yards and a quality 7:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio through West Virginia's first five games. The Mountaineers surrender 168.4 rushing yards per game, 108th in the country, and a shockingly bad 288.2 yards per game in the air - 133rd out of 138 FBS teams and only ahead of Stanford among P4 teams. Arizona, even without wideouts Gio Richardson, Chris Hunter, and Tre Spivey, moved the ball quite well against Cincinnati last week, and should have an even easier time doing so on Saturday - even on the road with an early 9:00 AM kickoff. West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona Wildcats game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 9, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football RichRod Week! It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. The Biggest Question: Can West Virginia's Defense Stop Anything? This West Virginia defense is just horrible. They gave up 577 yards to Iowa State last week, and are allowing a Big 12-worst 456 yards per game, which is 50 more yards per game than any other Big 12 team. They're dead last in passing and rushing yards allowed per game, and second-worst in points allowed per game. The Mountaineers are 100th in the nation in net yards per play (offense minus defense), and rank dead last in defensive efficiency in the league. OK, you get the point. So what is Rich Rodriguez and Zac Alley changing ahead of Saturday? It's not clear. But something needs to change. West Virginia vs. Arizona Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 35, West Virginia 31 The West Virginia Mountaineers are going to be desperate to avoid an 0-3 start in Big 12 play. They have the running game to keep this thing competitive, however, Arizona's front seven is underrated. One week after Cincinnati rushed for over 200 yards vs. Kansas State, they only mustered 74 yards on 28 carries for 2.6 yards per carry vs. Arizona. I don't believe Arizona will have that level of success vs. this WVU rushing attack, that has been the most-potent in the Big 12, but they'll do enough. And if Arizona can jump out to a lead and force Michael Hawkins Jr. to try and win a game through the air, that's a recipe for success. The only concern I have for Arizona is the travel and early kick at 12:00 p.m. CT, which will be a 9:00 a.m. kick for Arizona's body clock. Those games are always tough. However, if you're worried you're on an island with Arizona, don't be. The Wildcats are attracting 91% of the money wagered and have been bet up from -3 to -3.5 , indicating that both recreational and larger bettors are backing Arizona. Sometimes the obvious side is obvious for a reason. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. picks.headline: On SI Tulane Picks: Tulane vs Army
picks.blurb: On SI Tulane Picks: Tulane vs Army Skip to main content On SI Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Then, moving to the Crescent City, Doug did television PBP of Tulane games and even filled in for legendary Tulane broadcaster, Ken Berthelot in the only game Kenny ever missed while doing the Green Wave games. His father was an alumnus of Tulane in the 1940s, so Doug has attended Tulane football games in old Tulane Stadium, the Superdome, and Yulman. He was one of the 86,000 plus on December 1, 1973, sitting in the North End Zone to seeTulane shutout the LSU Tigers, 14-0. He was there when the Posse ruled Fogelman and in Turchin when the Wave made it to the World Series. He currently is the public address voice of the Tulane baseball team. picks.headline: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty October 9, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications American Conference Two high-powered rushing attacks meet in West Point for the first time since the 2024 American title game. Time and date: Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: CBS Sports Network Location: Michie Stadium — West Point, NY Spread: Army (-3.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Tulane leads, 14-10-1 Last meeting: Tulane 24, Army 17 — October 18, 2025 Current streak: Tulane, 1 (2025) Setting the scene Even before sharing the American Conference, Army and Tulane were famliar opponents, squaring off 19 times from 1996 through 2020. The Black Knights then joined the American in 2024 and instantly ran the league, rattling off an 8-0 conference record before handling Tulane in the conference championship game. That was the only time in the last four years Tulane didn’t serve as the conference title host. With first-year head coach Will Hall in the fold, the Green Wave hope to host the American Championship for a fourth time in five years. To achieve that goal, it starts with defeating Army at Michie Stadium in this conference opener. Tulane Green Wave outlook Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) split its non-conference slate, falling to Duke and Kansas State by double-digits on the road, while escaping Sun Belt opponents South Alabama and Southern Miss at home with late fourth quarter heroics. The biggest question entering this game, asks: who starts at quarterback? Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was Tulane’s Week 1 starter, but the Green Wave moved to Kadin Semonza for Weeks 2 through 4. But at the end of the last outing against Southern Miss, head coach Will Hall changed quarterbacks from Semonza to true freshman Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter. Johnson provided a spark in the come-from-behind victory, but his sample size remains small, completing just 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards without a single rushing attempt. The passing game unquestionably needs a boost. Tulane ranks 105th in the FBS in passing offense, completing just 54.2 percent of attempts with three touchdowns against one interception. The pass protection has been lacking too, allowing the 11th-most sacks per game in the country at 3.3. However, the Green Wave can dominate on the ground, and they do it with several different weapons. Running backs Jaylin Lucas and Maurice Turner each rushed for 200+ yards in the first four weeks, and the group gets even deeper as Jamauri McClure — Tulane’s starting running back during its 2025 College Football Playoff run — is slated to make his season debut. Tulane’s strength last season was its run defense, but the Green Wave have fallen off in that department, entering this matchup against the No. 1 rushing offense ranked 125th — allowing 191 yards per game on the ground. Losing star outside linebacker Chris Rodgers certainly doesn’t help, but the Green Wave still present veteran linebackers Makai Williams and Dickson Agu, who will be essential to countering this option. Army Black Knights outlook Army (2-2, 1-1 American) is already preparing for its third conference game. The Black Knights’ first two conference matchups were decided by the thinnest margins, featuring a lead change in the final two minutes. Army wound up on the wrong side of that late lead change in Week 2 when South Florida converted a late fourth down for a game-winning touchdown. But two weeks later, the Black Knights returned the favor at Temple. One-score games are customary for Army. Nine of the Black Knights’ last 10 matchups against FBS competition were decided by one score, and eight of the last nine were decided by four points or fewer — including every FBS matchup this season. Army’s option offense is in a familiar spot at first in the country in rushing yards per game at 334, while averaging the sixth-most yards per carry (6.4) in the FBS. Cale Hellums, who led all quarterbacks in rushing last year, remains the unit’s leading rusher with 301 yards, and his rushing performance dictates the result more than anyone else. In Army’s two wins, he has 191 yards and five touchdowns on a 6.6 average. In the losses to South Florida and Louisiana Tech, he combined for 110 yards and one touchdown on a 3.0 average. The Black Knights’ other ball carriers in the option attack include running back Godspower Nwawuihe and the explosive slot backs Samari Howard (293 rushing yards on a 10.9 average) and Zach Mundell (159 yards on a 14.5 average). However, Nwawuihe’s status remains unknown after he missed the Louisiana Tech game, which could make Carson Smith and Jake Rendina the downhill threats. Army’s defense allowed over 500 yards to Louisiana Tech, and that remains the team’s greatest struggle. The Black Knights are 89th nationally in yards allowed, while playing a style that typically limits possessions. Army has struggled with a lack of backfield pressure, producing the third-fewest sacks (3) and fewest tackles for loss (12) in the country. Additionally, the Black Knights are the only team yet to force a turnover. Army and Tulane are off to somewhat similar starts. Both are 2-2, highlighted by strong ground attacks and run defenses that need improvement. However, they sit on opposite sides of the time of possession spectrum, with Army ranking fourth nationally and Tulane third from the bottom. The Green Wave offense requires explosives in the run game, while the Black Knights move in a more methodical, sustainable fashion. Neither team is a proven passer, and Tulane may lean even more heavily on the run game than usual to keep its defense fresh. As usual, Army games come down to the wire. This will be no exception, and the Black Knights prevail at home in a low-scoring affair. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

Oklahoma looks to end its Red River Rivalry losing streak at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC) against Texas. The No. 1 Longhorns are a 7.5-point favorite, and my Texas vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football picks expect Steve Sarkisian's defense to shut down the Sooners yet again on Oct. 10. TOP PICK Who will win Texas vs Oklahoma: Texas -7.5 Recent Texas vs. Oklahoma rivalry history has been unkind to the Sooners, and I would take the Longhorns to cover as many as 9.5 points this year. Texas has beaten Oklahoma in three of Brent Venables' four Red River Rivalry games by an average of 32.3 points. In those three wins, the Longhorns held the Sooners to fewer than seven points, thanks to dominant defensive performances. This year's Texas defense might be the best one yet, ranking No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play , No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). Oklahoma's offense could struggle to put up double digits against Texas. The Sooners are averaging 12.3 points per game in their last three games and rank last in the SEC in offensive success rate (39.2%), largely due to John Mateer's poor play. Last year against Texas, Mateer was as bad as it gets (three interceptions, six turnover-worthy plays, 34.6 QBR). Texas vs Oklahoma Over/Under pick: Under 39.5 Texas and Oklahoma are 6-2 to the Under combined and have hit it in three of the last four Red River Rivalry games. When the Sooners' offense doesn't score, the Under tends to hit at the Cotton Bowl, and this year's OU offense doesn't score (I like the Under at 37.5 or better ). Oklahoma put up just 258 yards on Texas last year, and the Longhorns' defense is better this time around. It's ranked No. 5 by SP+ and has allowed more than 17 points once. That was to Ohio State and Heisman Trophy odds- favorite Jeremiah Smith, and it allowed just three points in the second half to the Buckeyes. However, it's not just Oklahoma's offense that has struggled. Texas is averaging 22 ppg against Power Four opponents, and Oklahoma's defense is still feisty. The Sooners are 12th in the country in havoc rate (21.6%), and Arch Manning has just one TD pass vs. two interceptions in P4 games. Texas vs Oklahoma combo The Red River Rivalry has been uncompetitive in three of Venables' four seasons in Norman. Oklahoma has a massive offensive problem, and there's no reason to believe this year will be any different. Mateer ranks 69th nationally in QBR (56.7) and has posted a 58.9 QBR or worse in three straight matchups, leading the Sooners to fewer than 300 total yards in each. OU's offense likely won't have its left tackle and is down one of its top receivers ( Trell Harris ) against a Texas defense that's allowing just 271 yards per game. However, the Sooners should slow Texas' offense down too. I have Texas winning Red River 24-13. picks.blurb: Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction by expert football model: Who wins the Red River Shootout? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of college football's great rivalry games renews this weekend as the Red River Shootout finds No. 1 ranked Texas facing off against Oklahoma in a critical test for both sides, if for very different reasons just a month into the 2026 season. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. What do the analytics department think of this week's matchup? For that, let's turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction: Can Arch Beat the Sooners' Defense? NCAA Football: Texas at Tennessee Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may not come as a surprise that the Longhorns are getting the favorite treatment against the Sooners, and by a decent margin, too. SP+ predicts that Texas will defeat Oklahoma by a projected score of 27 to 17 and will win the game by an expected margin of 9.9 points in the process. The model gives the Longhorns a very strong 73 percent chance of victory, one of the biggest discrepancies of any game this weekend. SP+ is a "tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency" that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring "the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football." How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Longhorns defend their No. 1 ranking? Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) in action during the game against the UTEP Miners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images That's a different question. Even with a Texas win, its place atop the AP poll could be in danger anyway as pollsters may be more impressed with what happens between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama as they face off in primetime. A big win over the Sooners could sway enough voters to stay at No. 1 , and everything looks like it should go the Longhorns' way. Even with questions around Arch Manning's continued development at the quarterback position. Sure, Texas is 4-0 and Manning looks much better than this time last year, but he has also clearly still not performed to expectations, either. Arch is a decent 63 percent passer but is making some curious decisions and doesn't look completely at ease in the pocket against better-quality fronts. Against an Oklahoma defense that, despite everything, remains one of college football's best – 4th against the pass, top 25 in scoring, and 3rd in third-down conversions – Manning could get seriously rattled early. But the Longhorns still have an advantage of their own on defense. They have battery of elite pass rushers who can wreck OU's blockers, shrink the pocket, and get at John Mateer on a regular basis. That should give the Texas offense enough chances to separate and pull away late. Horns by 10. What happens? Texas beats Oklahoma, and covers the spread. picks.headline: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend
picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 8, 2026 at 4:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners will take on the Texas Longhorns in the Red River Rivalry, and it could be closer than some think. The Oklahoma Sooners and Texas Longhorns have one of the biggest rivalries in sports. The Red River Rivalry is truly a spectacle . But the last few years haven't been as much of a game as we, as sports fans, have hoped for. This one could be the same way. Texas is the No. 1 team in the country. Oklahoma is no longer ranked, and shouldn't be. But Texas seems beatable despite being No. 1 overall. They could have lost to Tennessee not long ago. Yet the Sooners, with their baggage, still have a chance this weekend. However, not many are picking them to win. Final score predictions for Oklahoma vs. Texas Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame: Texas 21, Oklahoma 10 This feels like an ugly, low-scoring battle for much of the afternoon, with both defenses dictating the pace. Oklahoma's defense presents a major challenge for Texas, forcing Arch Manning to make a couple of crucial plays in difficult situations. Manning doesn't need to put up huge numbers, but he delivers when the Longhorns need him most and does just enough to keep the offense moving. Oklahoma's bigger issue is its offense, which struggles to sustain drives against a talented Texas defense. The Sooners find a few opportunities but can't capitalize enough to keep pace. Texas eventually creates some separation late, with Manning making the key throws to secure a hard-fought 21-10 victory in a game that never feels particularly comfortable for either side. Craig Smith , A to Z Tennessee: Texas 26 Oklahoma 9 I've watched Oklahoma a number of times this season, and I haven't seen many Power Four offenses worse than the Sooners' this year. I also haven't seen many defenses better than the Longhorns' this year. Colin Simmons is one of college football's most dominant defenders, totaling 5.5 sacks against Tennessee in one of the best overall defensive performances we've seen from a player and a team this season. Now, a floundering OU offense with no answers for getting John Mateer and the passing attack going will have to find a spark against one of the country's best defenses. I don't expect it will go any better than it did for the Sooners against Georgia. OU gives Texas some short fields, and that's all the Horns need to take control. Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida: Texas 19, Oklahoma 7 We've seen some wild things in Red River, and this game likely won't be an exception. The one thing that stands out is Oklahoma's offense. I don't trust what John Mateer is going to be able to do. He's gone from a fun quarterback at Wazzu to a player with a broken brain. I don't think Mateer will do much against the Longhorns, but I can see the defense getting the Sooners on the board because that unit can flat-out play. Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama: Texas 27, Oklahoma 19 Typically, Red River is one of the more anticipated games on the college football schedule, but that doesn't seem to be the case this year. That has little to do with Texas, however, as the No. 1-ranked Longhorns have held up their end of the hype deal; it has everything to do with Oklahoma, OU's offense, and John Mateer. The year-two leap at Oklahoma hasn't come to fruition, and Mateer may have regressed from how he looked pre-thumb injury to his current state. But I don't think it's all on Mateer. Oklahoma just doesn't have easy buttons on offense outside of Isaiah Stategna, and Ben Arbuckle hasn't exactly inspired much confidence with his scheme. I don't see a world where OU can score enough to keep up with the Longhorns. Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma: Texas 19, Oklahoma 13 The Oklahoma Sooners are in a bad spot right now. As we write this, they're dismissing their freshman wide receivers. But in other news, the offense is broken. And there's really no fixing it. However, the defense is still good enough to win them games. They just need decent play from the offense from time to time. I still don't think that happens this week. They're not healthy. Meanwhile, Texas looks good, especially on defense. Their offense can be efficient but has its own issues. This one is going to go to the Longhorns once again. For just the second time in the game's 126-year history, the Longhorns enter the game atop the Associated Press poll while the Sooners arrive unranked. Texas beat then-No. 1 Ohio State and picked up a hard-fought SEC road win two weeks ago at Tennessee. The Sooners have struggled so far with unimpressive wins over UTEP and New Mexico as well as losses at Michigan and Georgia. But a triumph in the Cotton Bowl could change the course of the season and take some heat off head coach Brent Venables, who's tallied a 34-22 record since taking over the OU program in 2022. The second straight win for a Texas team that had tied and lost in the first two weeks of the season kicked off the most dominant stretch in school history, which included a 30-game win streak and back-to-back national titles in 1969 and 1970. He's thrown for 883 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions and has just 76 yards rushing after picking up 1,255 yards and 23 touchdowns on the ground over the previous two seasons. WR Parker Livingstone , a 6-3, 200-pound junior, spent his first two years at Texas and even roomed with Longhorns QB Arch Manning. Livingstone transferred to Oklahoma during the offseason and has drawn some good-natured ribbing from Manning and Texas coach Steve Sarkisian, but he's had minimal impact for the Sooners with six catches through four games as well as a costly fumble against Michigan. OU's struggling offensive line ranks just 120th in the nation as a unit in Pro Football Focus's pass blocking grades, and the Longhorns rank fourth in the SEC with 15 sacks. If Mateer can't get protection, the Sooners may not reach the end zone for a fourth time in the past five games. The offensive line's struggles extend to the ground game. The Sooners average only 2.9 yards per carry, while the offense ranks last in the SEC in total offense with 321.3 yards per game. That doesn't bode well against a Texas defense that leads the SEC in scoring defense (13.3 ppg) and is fourth in total defense (271.0 ypg). Linebacker Rasheem Biles (30 tackles) and safety Jelani McDonald (26 tackles) both boast sideline-to-sideline range. That means Jackson, a 6-5, 275-pound sophomore, could get lots of one-on-one chances against E'Marion Harris opposite Simmons. Texas vs Oklahoma prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 26, Oklahoma 9.
