(Tom Fox/Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff Fri, October 9, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads During this week's Hear Me Out vodcast , our Kevin Sherrington asked if an Oklahoma victory would be the biggest upset in the history of this rivalry. While the panel of top scribes from San Antonio, Houston, Austin and Dallas came to no consensus, it is clear that the Sooners enter the game with a host of worries against a Texas team ranked No. 1. So, how does our group of experts see the 122nd edition of the Red River Rivalry? Kevin Sherrington Only twice has a No. 1 team ever lost in this rivalry, and both times it was Oklahoma, in 2008 and 1963. I don't see Texas making it three. Arch Manning hasn't exactly lit it up, but the Sooner Schooner is a wreck. Only Brent Venables' defense can keep it from being a blowout. Texas 24, Oklahoma 13 Shawn McFarland Brent Venables spoiled the X-factor of this week's game when he criticized the development of his offensive line. Against Texas' Colin Simmons and Co., with a weak offensive line and with a quarterback who struggles under pressure, this year's installment will mirror the last two. It might even be the worst of the three. Texas 31, Oklahoma 3 Lia Assimakopoulos These games are usually closer than expected, even when there's as large of a divide between the teams as it appears Texas and Oklahoma have this year. But the No. 1 Longhorns have already proved themselves against tough opponents like Ohio State and Tennessee, while the John Mateer-led Sooners have struggled against not only Georgia and Michigan, but even underwhelmed against New Mexico. Texas should take this one easily. Texas 24, Oklahoma 10 Oklahoma has had a week off to try and get things straight after being throttled by No. 2 Georgia in a turnover-filled mess. And the 'Dawgs don't have the pass rush that Texas does. John Mateer has had a rough enough start; can you imagine how bad things may go if Colin Simmons is constantly breathing down his neck? Texas 31, Oklahoma 13 The Sooners have failed to score a touchdown in three out of the last four Red River clashes. With the Oklahoma offense struggling, John Mateer spiraling and the Texas defense surging — not to mention the absence of Lewisville's Michael Fasusi, the anchor of the Sooners' O-line — they'll have just as much trouble finding the end zone on Saturday. Texas 27, Oklahoma 9 While anything can happen in a rivalry game, the No. 1 Longhorns should take care of Oklahoma (2–2) for the third straight year after winning at the Cotton Bowl 23-6 last season and 34-3 in 2024. Texas has already survived two tight games against tough competition — a 24-23 home win over Ohio State in Week 2 and a 20-17 road victory over Tennessee in late September — and junior edge Colin Simmons is playing like a first-round draft pick. The Duncanville product posted a Texas program-record 5.5 sacks during the win in Knoxville on Sept. 26 and made 2.5 against the Sooners last year. But Oklahoma won't make it easy on the Longhorns, as the Sooners try to bounce back from a 41-13 loss to Georgia in Week 4. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: ABC and ESPN Unlimited (Sean McDonough, Greg McElroy and Katie George) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) - National Radio: Compass Radio (Bill Jones and Tiki Barber) What You Need To Know DALLAS - The setting is familiar. The circumstances are not. Oklahoma and Texas meet for the 98th straight year Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT at the Cotton Bowl, and the Sooners listed as the designated home team. That is where the comfort ends. Texas is 4-0, ranked No. 1 in both major polls, and playing like the standard in the sport right now. Oklahoma is 2-2, unranked for the first time all season, and coming off a month that left more questions than answers. This is the Red River Rivalry with the roles flipped hard. The Sooners are not walking into Dallas as the hunted. They are walking in as the side that has to prove it still belongs in the same sentence. The degree of difficulty is historic enough on its own. Oklahoma just faced No. 2 Georgia . Now it gets No. 1 Texas . That makes this only the fourth time the Sooners have played the AP's top two teams in back-to-back games, joining 1963, 1987, and 2000. It is also just the fourth time since 2000 that any FBS team has drawn No. 1 and No. 2 in consecutive regular-season games. That is not a soft rivalry week. That is a measuring stick with no place to hide. The ranking split adds another layer. Since 2013, when one of these teams has been ranked and the other has not, the unranked side is 4-3. Oklahoma itself is only 3-4 against Texas since 1971 when entering the game unranked. Those numbers keep the door cracked open just enough to create hope. They do not change the larger truth. Texas is better right now, and Oklahoma has to play a near-perfect game to make this feel like a fight for four quarters. That starts on defense, because it has to. The Sooners still have a unit good enough to keep them alive. Oklahoma leads the nation by allowing just one passing touchdown and ranks among the national leaders in red-zone defense, first downs allowed, third-down defense, passing defense, and total defense. The identity is still there. The front can disrupt. The back end has been stingy. Every defensive starter through four games began his college career at Oklahoma , which matters in a rivalry game that usually rewards toughness and continuity more than portal gloss. The problem is that defense is going to be asked to cover for an offense that has not returned the favor. Oklahoma is averaging 22 points and barely more than 320 yards a game. The run game has been a mess. The offensive line has been inconsistent. John Mateer has had enough productive moments to stay in the conversation and enough damaging ones to keep the temperature high. He enters the week with 883 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and a 66.1 percent completion rate. That is fine on paper. The turnovers and stalled drives are why nobody in Norman feels fine about it. Across the field is Arch Manning , and that matchup alone would be enough to make this week heavy. Manning has 862 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions for a 4-0 Texas team that does not need the game script to get exotic to beat you. He can throw with velocity, process quickly, and hurt a defense with his legs if contain breaks down. Brent Venables already called him a player with no real weaknesses in the talent package. Oklahoma's best chance is not to eliminate him. It is to make him uncomfortable with interior pressure, late coverage disguise, and a physical perimeter. There are a few offensive crumbs the Sooners can point to. Mateer has already hit six touchdown passes of 20-plus yards this season. The tight end room has been more useful than expected under Jason Witten, especially Rocky Beers, who has 18 catches for 255 yards and has given Mateer a reliable intermediate option. Isaiah Sategna III remains the one receiver who can still change a drive by himself. That is not a complete offense. It is a group that has to become efficient enough to keep the defense from living in an impossible game script. Recent history does not help Oklahoma's nerves either. Last year's Red River game followed a familiar painful pattern: the Sooners hung around into halftime, then disappeared after it in a 23-6 loss. Texas controlled the third quarter, converted third downs, and turned a one-score game into a statement. Oklahoma had 12 tackles for loss that day and still could not get off the field often enough. That is the danger again this week. Play well in stretches and still lose the game in the moments that decide it.The larger backdrop is Year 3 in the SEC for both programs, and the contrast is getting harder to ignore. Texas looks like a national title contender. Oklahoma looks like a team still searching for offensive stability after a 10-win playoff season a year ago. The schedule has been brutal again, and it is not about to ease up after Dallas. But none of the remaining résumé talk matters if the Sooners cannot find a way to stay competitive against the top team in the country in the rivalry that still defines so much of the brand. Oklahoma's defense is good enough to give the game a pulse. Texas is complete enough to take it away in a hurry if the Sooners' offense stays stuck in the same place. Red River does not care about bye-week quotes, rankings debates, or how respectable the defensive profile looks on paper. It cares about which team imposes itself when the stadium is split down the middle and every possession feels louder than the last. Oklahoma needs clean football, a functional line, and a low-event afternoon from Manning. Texas needs to be itself. That is why this one feels so heavy.

away.headline: Initial injury report released for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma
away.blurb: For Texas, senior running back Hollywood Smothers remains off the injury report after sitting out against Tennessee with a lower-leg injury. Head coach Steve Sarkisian described the NC State transfer as an emergency option during that game. Still on the injury report after reportedly practicing last week is sophomore tight end Nick Townsend, who hasn’t played since suffering a bone bruise in his knee against Ohio State, but is now listed as probable. Less promising is the news with sophomore defensive lineman Justus Terry. The Georgia product sustained a toe injury warming up before the win over the Buckeyes, hasn’t played since, and is listed as doubtful along with sophomore wide receiver Kaliq Lockett, a new addition to the injury report. away.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? away.blurb: Well, this week's message is along that exact same vein, with the Horns' head coach denying to provide any additional context ahead of releasing the first availability report of the week, which comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday evening. Both were listed as "OUT" on the final availability report for Week 4 , alongside defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman. For now, one could hope (and reasonably assume, based on Sarkisian's message about getting healthier) that at least one of those players is ready for, or close to ready for, action in the rivalry game. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.headline: Oklahoma vs Texas: Key players listed on Wednesday Availability report
home.blurb: Most notable is that the guy who was supposed to start at left tackle, Michael Fasusi, doesn't look like he'll be available again this week. He started for the Sooners against UTEP but has missed the last three games with a shoulder injury. Fasusi is doubtful for the Red River Showdown. Also in question is the status of starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis. Pierre-Louis was listed as questionable going into Saturday. Joining the ranks of the unavailable this week are Xavier Robinson and Jacobe Johnson. Johnson suffered an injury during the loss to Georgia. Why Robinson isn't available is anyone's guess. He didn't get much playing time against the Bulldogs, logging just three snaps after getting nine snaps the week before against Michigan. Along with Fasusi, who is doubtful, are reserve backup tight end Trynae Washington and backup offensive lineman Fred Hinton. Washington has been a piece of Oklahoma's short-yardage formations, lining up in the backfield as a fullback for the Sooners. Their presence on the availability report is just another week where the Sooners will have question marks along the offensive line. Names to watch as the week moves along include linebacker Cole Sullivan, wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, safety Michael Boganowski, and tight end Jack Van Dorselaer. The Sooners need a spark this week if they want to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners are 1-3 against the Texas Longhorns under Brent Venables, and the offense hasn't scored a touchdown against their Red River rivals since 2023. Missing key members of the offensive line and the tight end room doesn't bode well for the Sooners' chances this Saturday. The 3-1 Ducks are already dealing with a thin margin for error as they prepare to host a 4-0 UCLA team that profiles as a potential dark-horse contender under first-year coach Bob Chesney. Both are coming off bye weeks following Week 4 wins, each impressive for different reasons. Oregon took down USC 41-27 on the road and showed an explosive offensive gear, even after losing starting quarterback Dante Moore to a scary injury in the first half. UCLA turned heads by traveling cross-country for a 54-3 win over Maryland , marked by an all-systems dominance which suggested the Bruins are no joke. While Chesney's first season since arriving from James Madison is off to a perfect start, this marks a new kind of challenge. The Bruins have not played a team currently ranked in the top 60 of the CBS Sports 138 and will be up against Oregon, which entered the season at No. 2 in the AP poll. After a stunning Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State , the Ducks began living up to preseason expectations in their Week 4 win over the Trojans. Oregon vs. UCLA: Need to know Dante Moore unlikely to play: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore returned to practice this week after suffering a concussion on a late hit in the first half of the Ducks' Week 4 win at USC. However, he's unlikely to play against UCLA. That should mean another opportunity for Dylan Raiola . The Nebraska transfer completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC and looked comfortable leading a talented Ducks offense. Having such a solid second option should reduce any urgency Oregon might feel to get Moore back on the field. Raiola is a former two-year starter for the Cornhuskers and a five-star prospect who is one of the nation's most talented second-string quarterbacks. UCLA's rushing attack : UCLA ranks No. 4 nationally in rushing offense at 281.5 yards per game on the ground. James Madison transfer Wayne Knight is the name to know. The 5-foot-7 speedster is tied for third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns. He reached the 100-yard mark in each of the Bruins' first two Big Ten games. Oregon is familiar with his game after he ran for 110 yards on 17 carries in the Ducks' 51-34 victory over James Madison in last year's College Football Playoff quarterfinal. The difference this time is that Knight has a better supporting cast around him. CFP implications: Oregon's Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State put the Ducks' postseason aspirations in early jeopardy. After UCLA, the only ranked opponent left on Oregon's schedule is Ohio State (Nov. 7). While having a manageable slate is helpful in some respects, there's also no guarantee the Ducks would make the CFP as an at-large team with two losses if there wasn't much meat on their resume. CBS Sports' College Football Forecaster projects Oregon with a 51.1% chance to make the 12-team field with a win over UCLA. That drops to 19.6% with a loss. UCLA would have a 33.3% chance to reach the CFP if it beats Oregon and an 8.3% chance with a loss. He was at the first practice this week, wearing a helmet and shoulder pads, according to coach Dan Lanning. Moore's next possible opponent would be the No. 21 UCLA Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten) , who are one of the three remaining undefeated Big Ten Conference programs. UCLA at Oregon's Updated Betting Odds The Week 6 matchup with the Southern California foe has Oregon still as a nearly two-touchdown favorite. According to FanDuel , the spread stands at 11.5. The Ducks' moneyline is -480 and the Bruins' is +360. The over/under is set at 58.5. The last time these two former Pac-12 Conference opponents met was in 2024, resulting in a 34-13 victory for Oregon in Pasadena, California. UCLA leads the all-time record, 33-40, dating back to 1928. The CBS matchup starts at 12:30 p.m. PT on Oct. 10 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon . Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana When speaking to the media back on Sept. 30, Lanning was quick to talk about the similarities that he has seen from the Bruins to last season's Big Ten and national champion, the Indiana Hoosiers. “They got some players that can play ball. Their running backs are as good as anyone who will go against them this year. They have a lot of players that came with them. And again, why I draw some comparisons to Indiana: a lot of guys that traveled with their coach right to the next stop.” First-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney brought offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy, defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, and fifth-year running back Wayne Knight along with him to sunny California after the James Madison Dukes of the Sun Belt Conference made the College Football Playoff last season. Their memorable run came to an end in the first round after a 51-34 loss to the Ducks in the Pacific Northwest on Dec. 21, 2025. “Extremely well-coached team," Lanning continued on about this year's Bruins. "You got two coordinators who were with him before, so they've been together for a while. They have a lot of continuity from that standpoint. They're running the ball as well as anybody in college football.” Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lanning Prepares to Deal With UCLA's Ground Game Lanning Prepares to Deal With UCLA's Ground Game Where the Ducks' defense needs to improve, in Lanning's mind, is in stopping explosive plays from UCLA's running barrage. Even the challenges that senior Nico Iamaleava presents through his aggressiveness on quarterback scrambles. On Oct. 5, Lanning reiterated to the media just how effective Chesney's offense is without an efficient passing game. "I would argue they have explosive runs; anytime you can run the ball in the end zone, I think they have more rushing touchdowns this year than they've had in the last two years combined," stated Lanning. Knight is one of the top ball carriers in the nation. He has already collected 445 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns (tied for the third-most in the sport). Slowing the star back down is the key to an Oregon winning effort over that confident unit in the backfield. "Against the run, I think we do a good job stopping runs between the tackles," Lanning explained back on Sept. 30. "However, we give up some big runs around the outside, and we need to do a better job defending and adjusting to those plays." picks.headline: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear
picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. McElroy picked against Oregon in Week 4, taking USC 34-31 before the Ducks won by 14 at the Coliseum. UCLA and Oregon kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Loading recommendations... I'm buying stock in Bruins first-year head coach Bob Chesney , who coached James Madison to a cover in a loss to the Ducks in the first round of the College Football Playoff last year. Oregon vs. UCLA scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks are the only team in the country to average over 300 passing yards per game without an interception, split between starter Dante Moore and backup Dylan Raiola. Oregon ranks third nationally in passing yards per game and has done a good job of avoiding turnovers. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The Ducks rank toward the back half in the country around 4.6 yards per rushing attempt. If the Bruins can establish their ground game and control the tempo of this game, they'll have a chance to spring an upset. picks.blurb: ESPN's Playoff Predictor Says the Ducks Must Win Against UCLA - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 ESPN's Playoff Predictor Says the Ducks Must Win Against UCLA (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Anthony Moeglin Fri, October 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks have put themselves into a spot that they absolutely must win on Staurday afternoon against the UCLA Bruins. Thanks to their loss against the Oklahoma State Cowboys, the Ducks have just a 39 percent chance to make the College Football Playoffs, and their schedule going forward is a big reason why. Not only do they have this marquee matchup against UCLA , but they have huge games against Northwestern and Ohio State to end the season. If they go undefeated the rest of the way, it is likely that they will be a top-four seed in the tournament and get a bye week. However, there are plenty of reasons to believe that they wouldn't be able to do that. In every one of their games so far, the Ducks' defense has left a lot to be desired. They have given up at least 27 points to each of their opponents except Portland State, whom they beat 84-0. Success has clues, but so does failure, and the Ducks have a very long way to go to be considered one of the best teams in the country. The first step in that process is beating the UCLA Bruins on Saturday. If it were one of the past 10 years, this game would be a foregone conclusion. Instead, the 2026 version of the UCLA Bruins is a very legit group and a team that commands attention and respect. The Bruins come into the game on Saturday with a perfect 4-0 record, ranked No. 21 in the country. They do a lot of things right, and they play extremely hard, which makes them nearly impossible to beat. The turnaround that Bob Chesney has orchestrated has been nothing short of spectacular, and they are playing that way. Oregon is between a rock and a hard place . They have to show up; their postseason lives depend on it, and as much as I don't want to say this in Week 5, this is a must-win for the Oregon program. If Oregon wants to get where they want to go, they cannot slip up against the UCLA Bruins; it is as simple as that. One more loss against an inferior opponent will put the nail in the coffin for this season. The reverse is also true, UCLA is a quality enough opponent that a win against them can catapult them back into the top-10 and allow them to stay alive for the rest of the season.

We have previewed Lane Kiffin's offense and Blake Baker's defense, as the Tigers have high level talent all over the field. We also laid out Kentucky's path to victory in this football game. It will take the Wildcats best shot to take down the Tigers, here are my final thoughts and prediction. A lot of people are overlooking LSU's side of the injury report as they are without two All-American level players in tight end Trey'Dez Green and linebacker Whit Weeks, the Tigers will also be without starting nickel Dashawn Spears. Kentucky is down linebacker depth in a big way, as Alex Afari, Tavion Wallace and Antwan Smith are all out for this game. Kentucky is also down their backup nickel Jaden Smith, but the starting nickel Aaron Gates returns after missing last week. Kentucky is at full strength offensively, running back Jason Patterson and wide receiver DJ Miller are both ready to go. We have talked all week about the crossover between these two teams; the long relationship between Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker. Louisiana product and breakout true freshman Kenny Darby was committed to LSU at one time. Kentucky has multiple players that were at LSU at one point in their career: left tackle Lance Heard, wide receiver Nic Anderson and defensive tackle Ahmad Breaux. There is one crossover we have not mentioned this week... LSU has a familiar face leading their offensive line, that is coach Eric Wolford. Coach Wolford could not revive the big blue wall during his two stints in Lexington. LSU has a lot of talent on the offensive line, left tackle Jordan Seaton is one of the top NFL Draft prospects at his position. However, that unit has had some rough outings this season (shocking) and the interior offensive line is gettable; Kentucky's defensive line has to win the line of scrimmage and get pressure on quarterback Sam Leavitt. Another area of the game we have yet to mention is how good Kentucky has been in the "middle 8", these are the last four minutes of the first half and the first four minutes of the second half. Kentucky leads the country in points per drive on offense in the middle 8 and this has to continue in this game. The defense for the Wildcats have performed much better in the middle 8 as well. You can look at the graph of full FBS teams below, this is something to watch closely on Saturday. Kentucky just has to play their style of football to win this game, granted they have to do it almost flawlessly to come away with a massive victory. Kentucky has to win the turnover margin, which is something they have consistently done this season. The defense has been very opportunistic and the Wildcats have done a phenomenal job at staying on schedule offensively. Kentucky can utilize their unique offensive scheme to move the football and score points, but the Wildcats have to create explosives on this Blake Baker defense that allows explosives. Kentucky has done really well on a few areas defensively. The Wildcats rank 6th in the SEC in EPA per dropback allowed and explosive play rate allowed. Kentucky also ranks 2nd in the conference in turnover forced percentage. If Kentucky can limit explosives for the Tigers and create explosives on offense, they will be in a great position to win this football game. It is worth noting that Kentucky is 5-0 against the spread in their last five meetings against top ten teams, and they have won three of those games outright as underdogs. LSU is not at full strength, down both players that had the honor of wearing the legendary number 7 in the Tigers program. Kentucky is closer to full strength as the starting 22 is healthy and ready to go for this one. This is a game that I originally predicted a loss for the Wildcats, but I think Kentucky has a ton of momentum right now and will benefit from an incredible atmosphere at Kroger Field. picks.headline: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule
picks.blurb: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 Story by Wildcats Wire LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:53 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football hosts a top ten team in the LSU Tigers under the lights of Kroger Field, and the bluegrass is as fired up as ever coming off the largest comeback road win in program history. The energy is at an all time high in Lexington, as Will Stein has kicked off his first year as head coach with a 4-1 record. Kentucky was dropped out of the AP top 25 after their road win at South Carolina, this will add some motivation as this is just the third time since 2000 a team was dropped from the top 25 following a win. We previewed Lane Kiffin's dynamic offense he is bringing with him, now it is time to preview the Tigers defense that is statistically one of the best in the conference. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker was retained by Kiffin as he has done a phenomenal job with the Tigers defense. This is a defense loaded with talent, but will unfortunately be without the leader and green dot in Whit Weeks. LSU gave up 32 points on the road at Ole Miss, they have allowed just 44 total points in their other four games combined. That game was big for a lot of reasons, but when you look at the statistics per secstatcat.com; Kentucky and Ole Miss have very similar numbers offensively. Kentucky - SEC Rank Ole Miss - SEC Rank Early Down Conv. % Ole Miss, similar to Kentucky, has also struggled on converting 3rd downs this season. Ole Miss has definitely been better on third downs, but is still an area they need to improve on. Both Kentucky and Ole Miss have canceled out their third down woes by converting on early downs. They are first and second in the SEC in converting on early downs, and they join Georgia and Alabama as the only SEC teams that are converting over 50% on early downs. This is an area Kentucky has to continue to have success in to win this game, staying on schedule is a huge factor in this football game. Kentucky cannot get in 3rd and long as that is when LSU can overwhelm you with the talent they have on the defensive line. Princewill Umanmielen followed Kiffin over from Ole Miss and he is a true game wrecker off the edge. Umanmielen leads all of college football with eight sacks on the season, this will be a true test for both tackles Lance Heard and Malachi Wood. Another interesting aspect of this matchup is the relationship of Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker. They worked together for years at Louisiana Tech and obviously spent the last couple of season together at LSU. They know each other really well, and they could know tendencies of each other as play callers that could create advantages in certain situations. Sloan knows a good amount of the roster at LSU, and it is intriguing to see if that can pose advantages for the Wildcats. The LSU defense has been incredible against the pass game, as they lead the SEC in EPA/dropback allowed. Their secondary is led by corner DJ Pickett and safety Ty Benefield, both players are NFL Draft prospects that can make plays at every level of the field. Their starting slot corner Dashawn Spears tore his ACL and is out for the season. This has led Ty Benefield to playing that spot in nickel formations, and he will have his hands full with Louisiana native, breakout true freshman slot receiver Kenny Darby This will be an extra special game for a lot of people on Kentucky's offense. Offensive coordinator Joe Sloan was fired as offensive coordinator at LSU before making the move to Lexington. Kenny Darby broke high school receiving records in the state of Louisiana and was committed to LSU for a long time. Wide receiver Nic Anderson also transferred over from LSU. Kentucky's offense will continue to be difficult for opposing defenses, as the scheme just constantly forces you to communicate. This LSU defense has a ton of playmakers, but Kentucky can find success as long as they stay on schedule. Kentucky is one of the best offenses in creating yards before contact and the offensive line has been steady in pass protection all season. The Wildcats offensive line has to find a way to win the line of scrimmage in this game, and it is easier said than done with this stout LSU defensive line. Kentucky will have to find success on offense to win this football game. Expect Lane Kiffin and Charlie Weis to put points on the board as they always do. This is a defense similar to Alabama, where Kentucky struggled to consistently move the football on in week two. There is no doubt the Wildcats offense has improved since then, but we will see just how much they have improved on Saturday. home.headline: Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable'
home.source: California Golden Bears On SI on MSN
home.blurb: The Bears (2-3, 1-1 ACC) return home Saturday to face Virginia Tech (3-2, 1-1) in a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Memorial Stadium. Will JKS miss his first game in two seasons or could he return to face the Hokies? We don’t know. Turns out Sagapolutele continued to show “some symptoms” during the second half and he now is among four Cal players undergoing multiple tests every day as part of the Bears’ concussion protocol program. Safety Kingston Lopa is also facing those protocols, Lupoi said. Besides Lopa going out with the head injury, the Bears played portions of the UNLV game without defensive backs Cam Sidney and Daniel Harris, both ejected after targeting penalties. Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is among 10 Cal starters dealing with injuries — one of four in concussion protocol — coach Tosh Lupoi reported Tuesday. Cal is not required to provide details about injuries, although we will get status updates when the ACC releases its initial player availability chart on Wednesday night. We do know this much: Cal football athletic director and general manager Ron Rivera was not happy with the play that led to Sagapolutele leaving the game in the final minute of the half at UNLV. Rivera called the injury “avoidable.” Cal was trailing 24-7 when JKS rolled right and threw incomplete on first-and-10 from his own 25-yard line. UNLV linebacker Elias Rudolph, a transfer from Miami, flung Sagapolute to the artificial turf and the sophomore QB’s bounced off the artificial turf. No flag was thrown, but Rivera clearly believed that should have happened. “JKS’s concussion, in my opinion, was avoidable. And I agree with Tosh, something should have happened,” he said. “When the quarterback throws the ball and the defender sees him throw the ball, there’s no reason to allow him to violently grab a guy and swirl around him and throw him to the ground. "Just go back and watch the tape. That’s all I’m going to say about that.” Lupoi removed Sagapolutele from the game after watching him stagger back to the huddle. At halftime, he was told JKS was cleared to play, but Lupoi said he didn’t feel comfortable sending him back onto the field. With backup Jackson Brousseau performing well at quarterback, Cal rallied to take a 25-24 lead in the second half before the Rebels answered to win 39-31. The closest Lupoi came to providing a hint as to whether Sagapolutele might face Virginia Tech was when he offered, “He was cleared to go back in at one point. That tells you it was a minor whatever-you-want-to-call-it.” Cal already has been playing without injured running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas. The Bears were desperate enough at the position that wide receivers Tyree Sams and Carson Perry-Smith were given snaps — and carries — at running back in Saturday. “You may or may not see that this week,” Lupoi said. One of the biggest games of the college football season is at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) when Georgia and Alabama play for the 10th time in the Kirby Smart era. The Crimson Tide are 1.5-point home favorites with College GameDay in town, and given Smart's struggles against them, my Georgia vs. Alabama prediction and college football picks project Kalen DeBoer's program to win a defensive battle in the downpour. Who will win Georgia vs Alabama: Alabama ML Kirby Smart has historically struggled against Alabama , and I like the Crimson Tide to cover up to -1.5 , but would rather play it safe and take the Tide to win. Since taking over Georgia in 2017, Smart is 2-7 straight up against the Crimson Tide and 0-3 in the regular season since 2020. With the Georgia vs. Alabama weather report calling for heavy rain and strong winds, this game will likely be low-scoring and come down to which offense can make more explosive plays late. That gives the Crimson Tide the advantage, with Keelon Russell ranking third nationally in QBR (91.0) and Alabama's offense being 12th in the country in offensive success rate (51.2%). Georgia's defense hasn't faced an offense as loaded as Alabama's this season. And against the lone quality defense Georgia QB Gunner Stockton has faced ( Oklahoma ), he struggled (65.7 QBR, 60.9% adjusted completion rate). TOP PICK Georgia vs Alabama Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The weather is expected to be as big a factor in this being a low-scoring game as these elite defenses. The game total has dropped from 56.5 to 51.5 (I like the Under at 51.5 or better ), with Hurricane Isaias expected to make landfall near Alabama on Friday. College GameDay even announced it's relocating Saturday morning's show inside due to the weather in Tuscaloosa. There's an 83% chance of precipitation with wind gusts of 19 mph at kickoff, which will only help these defenses shine. Alabama's defense is ranked top 25 nationally in havoc rate (20%) and success rate (37.9%), while Georgia's defense is the best Russell has faced and maybe the best in the country. The Bulldogs' defense is ranked No. 1 by SP+ . Georgia vs Alabama combo This is by far the No. 1 must-watch game in my college football Top 25 predictions this week, and the weather adds an extra wrinkle. Points will be hard to come by, especially early, as these offenses adjust to the wet conditions. However, the Crimson Tide have the advantage on offense with their QB. Russell is more dynamic than Stockton and has been on another level in his last three games, with 13 total touchdowns and a 96.7+ QBR in each outing. He can make the difference late in a low-scoring game. Georgia vs Alabama Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats
picks.blurb: Georgia vs Alabama Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Mike Ditka dies at 86 Buccaneers stun Cowboys Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' NFL injury tracker updates Guardians force Game 5 Vaughn Dalzell Wed, October 7, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The two highest scoring teams in the country are the #6 Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0) and #2 Georgia Bulldogs (5-0); and lucky for us, they play Saturday night in primetime! Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . "Going back to Iowa State, they've always used their tight ends really well, and they're doing so here [Penn State]. Defensively, they look a lot like the past Penn State teams in being big up front," Riley said during his Oct. 5 appearance on Trojans Live. Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game against USC, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer The last couple of weeks have set off some serious alarms for me about Penn State, and that does not fill me with a great amount of confidence in the Nittany Lions going into this matchup against USC. The Trojans have struggled with the defense this season but I'm not seeing the firepower necessary to keep things too competitive with the Trojans on Saturdya night. After Northwestern ran all over Penn State's defense, I think the Trojans would be smart to try mimicking that with King Miller setting the tone on the ground and allowing Jayden Maiava to do his thing with the passing game. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt of USC will be a problem all nigth for the Penn State defense. Final score prediction: USC 27, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Jayden Maiava, USC quarterback Paul White, Contributor This hurts to predict, but I just don't see a way Penn State wins this game. The offense should be able to get back on track against a weaker defense, but if we couldn't stop Northwestern's offense, then I'm terrified to see what USC does. Final score prediction: USC 38, Penn State 27 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor It feels like the gig is up for the Nittany Lions. What should be a celebration of one of college football's greatest modern traditions could turn into a State College massacre. I don't think that there will be much resistance from the blue and white, but I could see young edge talent Yvan Kemajou flashing some potential. Penn State was blown out by Northwestern last week, with the team performing poorly on both sides of the ball. After three straight wins to open the year, the Nittany Lions are now back to the drawing board for ways to right the ship. Head coach Matt Campbell will have to get his guys back on track, and the schedule-makers didn't do them any favors this week. Penn State will be hosting the USC Trojans this weekend, giving the team a chance to take on a top-20 opponent. This matchup will test the Nittany Lions, seeing how they can perform against one of the top teams in the country. Penn State will try to pull off the upset, and if they can, the last few weeks will be more of a blip on the season. Coming into the game, Penn State is being favored to win, at least by ESPN's game predictor . The Nittany Lions have been given a 62 percent chance to upset the Trojans, earning a massive win at home. Penn State may be favored in the game due to the game being played at home, with the Nittany Lions having a strong home-field advantage. But this team does have talent, and despite the two losses in a row, this matchup gives them an opportunity to showcase it. Quarterback Rocco Becht will be the key in this game, and he is going to need to put together a better performance this week. Becht has struggled in each of the past two games, leading to the losses for the Nittany Lions. While the struggles from Penn State aren't all on his shoulders, Becht does make a big difference to this team. For the season, the veteran signal-caller has thrown for 1,108 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Against an opportunistic Trojans defense, Becht will need to limit his turnovers, keeping the ball with the offense. USC has a strong offensive-attack, and if they are given more opportunities or shirt fields, it may be a tough game for Penn State. Penn State has the means to pull off an upset win against the Trojans in this game, and if they can, they could build momentum for the rest of the season. (Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jared Slanina Thu, October 8, 2026 at 11:07 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nittany Lions seek their first win in Big Ten play after stumbling to an 0-2 start. in conference play. Penn State (3-2, 0-2) vs. USC (5-1, 2-1) Kickoff: 7:30 p.m., Beaver Stadium, State College, PA The Betting Line: Penn State -1.5 (Fanduel) TV: NBC, 7:30 p.m., Noah Eagle (play-by-play), Todd Blackledge (analyst), Kathryn Tappen (sideline) Weather: A cloudy day with a high of 67, with temps dropping into the upper 50s during the evening. Matt Campbell: PENN STATE RECORD: 3-2, 1st Year OVERALL RECORD: 110-72, 15th Year Lincoln Riley: USC RECORD: 40-19, 5th Year OVERALL RECORD: 95-29, 9th Year VS. PENN STATE: 0-1 Tony Rojas is the only active player with more than 21 career TFLs and six career interceptions…Saturday will be the 19th full stadium white out in Beaver Stadium history…USC and Penn State are both in the top 10 in program wins and winning percentage…USC leads the all-time series 6-5 over Penn State…the two programs will be meeting for the second time as members of the Big Ten. Jayden Maiava is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation when he heats up. The likely future first round draft pick has continually improved in three years as a starter, and is enjoying his best season up to this point. He is completing 69% of his passes with 15 touchdowns and three interceptions, and is on pace to set career highs in just about every category. Maiava has accomplished this without wide receiver Trent Mosely, who was quickly establishing himself as one of the nation's best receivers as a true freshman. He has been out with an injury since week two, and is not likely to return on Saturday. The Trojans still have their typical number of playmakers at the skill positions. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, a freshman with the body of a veteran NFL receiver, has become the primary targets with 25 catches for 372 yards and three scores. Zacharyus Williams, another big-bodied receiver, has been a dangerous deep threat and is coming off his best game. Maiva also looks to tight end Mark Bowman often, a freshman who has become more involved with the offense in recent weeks – although he is questionable with an undisclosed injury. King Miller returns to the USC offense after rushing for just under 1,000 yards as a true freshman. He came back bigger and faster, and can be hard to take down at 6-0, 225 lbs. He can also be dangerous in the open field despite his size, and has a run of at least 20 yards in each of the past four games. Waymond Jones is another big, physical back who excels in short yardage situations. Penn State's defense appeared to be the strength of the team, and one of the best in the Big Ten. However, that sentiment was erased by Northwestern on Friday in of the poorest defensive performances in recent memory. The Wildcats put up 406 rushing yards, averaging 7.5 yards with each carry. Northwestern was able to run so freely that they only had 14 passing attempts while controlling the clock. It doesn't help that they will be facing a coach in Lincoln Riley that excels at creating offensive gameplans, and was just handed a blueprint for how to move the ball on the defense. It's hard to find any current point of optimism for the Penn State offense. The tackles have been unable to set the edge. The interior line is unable to open up running lanes or keep the pocket clean. The running backs have failed to find explosive plays, or provide a consistent ground game. Tight end Andrew Rapplyea and center Brock Riker are both playing through injuries that are obviously limiting their play. The receivers have shown promise, but don't get many chances because of all the off-target passes and balls regularly getting knocked down at the line of scrimmage. Rocco Becht has not yet shown he is capable of moving the ball against a Big Ten defense through two games. Despite being the nation's most experienced quarterback, he has often looked lost within the offense once the level of competition improved. Fortunately for Penn State, they are facing a defense that has been struggling after a positive start in non-conference play. The Trojans are ranked 14th or worse in the Big Ten in scoring defense, pass defense, total defense, and explosive plays allowed. USC gave up 30 points against Louisiana, 35 against Rutgers and 41 to Oregon in consecutive weeks. They are coming off a better result against a Washington offense decimated by injuries, holding them to 21 points and a key stop in the final minute to preserve the victory over the Huskies. If Penn State can find some rhythm, it may be against this defense. Safety Christian Pike is USC's most productive player, and should be on an NFL roster next season. He leads the team with 35 tackles, and has an interception and two pass breakups. Similar to Penn State, USC has a pass rush by committee and do not seem to have a dominate pass rusher who regularly makes plays in the backfield. Penn State fans will also recognize a couple of former Nittany Lions who transferred to USC over the off-season in linebacker Ta'Mere Robinson and defensive end Zuriah Fisher. SPECIAL TEAMS USC kicker Caden Chittenden is 6-of-7 on the season, with a career-long of 52 yards in 2024 while playing at UNLV. Punter Lachlan Carrigan is as consistent as they come, and has an average of 49.3 yards per punt. Penn State kicker Ryan Barker missed his second field goal of the season on Friday after not missing a single field goal that was not blocked in 2025. Barker has a career high of 49 yards, which he has hit on multiple occasions. Punter Nathan Tiyce is averaging 41.6 yards per punt this season, and is coming off a shaky performance against Northwestern with several short kicks. USC-27, Penn State-17 Maybe Penn State is able to prove they are better than the team we've watched in the last two weeks. Maybe there are some quick fixes to set things right. But for now, it appears the Nittany Lions are lost and searching for answers that may never come. It could be this team just isn't good enough to beat a quality opponent. Penn State will likely come out fighting and be boosted by the White Out crowd. However, my prediction comes to one simple fact – USC's offense can move the ball. Penn State still hasn't proven they can do so.

away.blurb: Washington suffered a neck injury during spring practice and was due to be re-evaluated last week. Fisch said on Monday that it looks like the Huskies will not get the third-year runner back in action for a long while, however, so it's probably safe to assume that Washington is out for the season. Moss will not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a soft-tissue injury on the first play of the Washington State game. Chris Lawson has started three games in his absence at the X receiver position and is second on the team in receiving with 13 catches for 212 yards and a touchdown. Fisch said this week that their understanding is that Moss, a sixth-year senior, will be out of eligibility due to the NCAA eliminating injury waivers with the advent of 5-in-5 eligibility beginning this season. Carr will also not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a hand injury against Washington State that required surgery. He had 5 carries for 28 yards before the injury, which opened the door for Limar to lead the Huskies backfield in the second half. With Carr, Limar, and Washington all out, freshman Brian Bonner Jr. and sixth-year Trey Cooley will continue to split reps in the Huskies backfield. Christian tore his Achilles during spring practice and is out for the season. He has remained around the team, but like Moss, will likely be out of eligibility after the year even with the injury wiping out his season. C Landen Hatchett - GAME-TIME DECISION Fisch revealed this week that Hatchett had a second surgery on his wrist in the spring after initially going under the knife in December to heal what the fourth-year center called a scaphoid fracture when talking to the media this spring. After that second surgery, Fisch told the media that the impression was that Hatchett would be available by the second-to-last week of fall camp, but the process to get him cleared for contact has taken longer than they hoped. Hatchett suited up against Minnesota but was ruled out on the gameday report, but Fisch said that he would be a game-time decision this week. Karnley pulled up limping on a long touchdown the Huskies allowed to Utah State and missed the rest of that game, Eastern Washington, and Minnesota. He was suited up against Minnesota, however, and defensive coordinator Ryan Walters told sideline reporter Dave Mahler that Karnley was available in an emergency situation. The fourth-year corner was upgraded to probable on Friday's injury report and should be good to go this afternoon. The Huskies still have one looming question on their gameday injury report, however. He had 12 carries for 50 yards and a touchdown against the Cougars before exiting.

USC Trojans lose starting wide receiver for season with knee injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Worker to Dak: 'Embarrassing' USC Trojans lose starting wide receiver for season with knee injury JD McCarthy, College Sports Wire Sat, October 3, 2026 at 2:31 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The USC Trojans will be without starting wide receiver Corey Simms for the rest of the season after he suffered a knee injury, according to Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer of CBS Sports. Simms played USC's first four games of the season before missing last week's game against the Oregon Ducks . He made the first three starts os his career before his season came to an early end. The sophomore is fourth on the team with 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown. He had the best game of his career against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, catching four passes for 72 yards and the first touchdown of his career. He played in all 13 games last year as a true freshman, but his biggest contributions were on special teams, with him catching just one pass for six yards. USC (4-1, 1-1 Big Ten) is looking to bounce back from its 41-27 loss to Oregon on Saturday when they host the Washington Huskies (3-1, 0-1). home.blurb: However, Mosley is not the only USC player dealing with an injury concern as the Trojans prepare for their challenging matchup. USC's latest injury report lists four players as out for the game, including wide receiver Corey Simms, safety Kendarius Reddick, linebacker Roman Marchetti, and offensive lineman Kilian O'Connor. Mosley is one of six Trojans currently listed as questionable. Apart from him, wide receiver Terrell Anderson, tight end Mark Bowman, offensive lineman Hayden Treter, and defensive tackles Jahkeem Stewart and Jide Abasiri have also been listed as questionable alongside Mosley. The Big Ten's availability reports will continue to receive updates as the teams move closer to kickoff. USC will therefore keep monitoring Mosley's condition throughout the remainder of the week before determining whether the talented wide receiver is healthy enough to make his return against Penn State.
